A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with matching methods, applications, and appendices A.1–A.7. Their text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support reliable comparison, including identification of relocated and removed material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian simulations, hierarchical AR(1) experiments, and analyses of synthetic and real fluorescence lifetime imaging data.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds baseline outcomes, damping optimization results, and fluorescence posterior-predictive analyses.

M1.justification: v1 uses exponential damping; v2 additionally introduces a flexible damping family with two shape parameters and optimizes it during inference (Section 4.2). The hierarchical factorization, score networks, training objectives, mini-batch estimator, and adaptive sampling framework remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian task, hierarchical AR(1) grids up to 128×128, and synthetic and real fluorescence imaging data. The additional baseline results and decay-tail diagnostics reuse this coverage; no new domain, population, or inference task is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds an evaluated GAUSS baseline from Linhart et al. (2024), which v1 only discussed. The NUTS comparison also gains results at 128×128, previously marked N/A. The other samplers and the fluorescence MLE comparator are retained.

E3.justification: Table 1 adds a 30-minute per-dataset limit to the existing 10,000-step budget. New protocols cover flexible damping optimization and fluorescence R² and posterior-predictive evaluation, including 100 simulations and decay-tail masking. Appendix A.5 also revises the stated Gaussian covariance from sigma I to sigma² I; unchanged retained plots do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends supplementary validation through flexible damping optimization, a qualitative comparison of fixed versus regenerated training simulations, and fluorescence predictive checks examining coverage and decay-tail discrepancies. It removes v1 Figure 10's NUTS recovery and calibration diagnostics. Existing damping, mini-batch, noise-schedule, and conditioning analyses are retained, including the relocated AR(1) damping plot.

E5.justification: Both versions retain ten-run reporting with medians and median absolute deviations; Table 2's mean and standard deviation convention was already stated in v1. v2 adds explicit 95% posterior-predictive intervals, coverage reporting from 100 simulations, and posterior-predictive p-value estimation. No increase in independent repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: The empirical record gains GAUSS convergence outcomes and NUTS 128×128 results: global/local RMSE 0.01/0.09 and contraction 1.00/0.99 replace N/A in Table 2. Newly reported fluorescence mean R² is 0.961 versus 0.871 for MLE; mean predictive p-values are 0.20 and 0.40 after tail masking. v2 also reports flexible-damping outcomes and revises runtime claims. Section 4.1 corrects the stated successful damping factor from 0.003 to 0.1, while Figure 2 and the other retained performance plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a formal posterior-predictive discrepancy and Monte Carlo p-value definition. Appendix A.5 corrects and expands the Gaussian model specification and supplies its explicit posterior mean and precision. The central SDE formulation and mini-batch unbiasedness proposition and proof remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: simulation-efficient hierarchical inference, stable compositional sampling, and error-damping mini-batch estimation at very large scales. The three applications and the claim of handling over 750,000 parameters remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds density/process mismatch to its instability explanation, qualifies NUTS practicality, and interprets fluorescence predictive discrepancies as partly decay-tail related. It also discusses limitations of the optimization criterion for multimodal posteriors. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit qualification that choosing d0 below one does not theoretically recover the true posterior.

D1.justification: v2 documents Optuna optimization and search ranges, the sbi GAUSS implementation, BayesFlow diagnostics, individual training times, and NUTS hardware. It also specifies 100 held-out synthetic fluorescence images. Most architecture and training details are retained. However, v1's code/data access paragraph and repository link are removed, and the earlier statement identifying the hyperparameter-search data as a test dataset is no longer provided.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Optuna, the sbi toolkit, and the BayesFlow workflow software. It narrows the SDE positioning from absence in prior compositional work to absence in most prior work, removing Gloeckler et al. from that particular exclusion while retaining the citation elsewhere. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Section 3 is substantially rewritten and reordered so stabilization precedes hierarchical construction. The compositional explanation and parameter notation are revised, and the experiments receive consistent setup, baseline, and results organization with extensive paragraph editing. These changes substantially reshape the explanatory sequence.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, moves the overview figure earlier, and merges the AR(1) damping plot into the appendix ablation figure. The main fluorescence figure is redesigned with predictive bands and R² maps, and its appendix comparison gains predictive-curve and p-value panels. The standalone NUTS diagnostic figure is removed, and Table 1 gains a comparator row.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports the existing empirical claims through the GAUSS comparison, measured large-grid NUTS results, and quantitative fluorescence predictive checks. The reorganized method explanation also improves clarity. These gains are bounded: calibration limitations remain, while the code/data access information, NUTS calibration figure, and explicit d0 below one qualification are removed. Overall, the added evidence yields a limited net improvement rather than resolving the paper's central reliability limitations.
